title: Finite Gibbs spectral-tail energy Markov audit
question: Can the local Gibbs spectral complement be bounded by positive shifted-energy moments at every finite cutoff, providing the missing quantitative input for the cutoff-aware two-stage shell route?

model.local_energy: K_W=H_W-min(spec(H_W)) I on each contiguous W-site core, so K_W is positive semidefinite
model.analytic_target: prove a cutoff-independent moment bound and combine it with the QCMI high-cutoff plateau to control the Gibbs spectral complement

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks scalar Markov inequalities and positivity; finite spectral projectors, Gibbs moments and cutoff limits remain Python/open analysis.

qft_interface.closed: On the finite declared grid, positive shifted local energy moments dominate both mass and energy-weighted spectral tails at every sampled cutoff and threshold.
qft_interface.open: Finite Markov inequalities do not supply cutoff-independent moment bounds. Uniform Gibbs complement control, shell summability, source/volume/shape uniformity, beta/eta independence, common core, Cook/common-alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary finite spectral-tail interface only; no physical-sector conclusion or production-owner transfer is supplied.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite Gibbs spectral-tail energy audit only. It proves no cutoff-independent moment bound, shell modulus, Gibbs complement theorem, volume/source/shape bound, common core, beta/eta-independent topology, domain or Cook/common-alpha convergence, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A result.
